heard: Three men are the only humans to have ever died in space. Most people assume space fatalities happen during fiery rocket launches or high-altitude explosions. In June 1971, Soyuz 11 launched carrying Georgi Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsiev. The crew successfully docked with Salyut 1, setting new space endurance records over three weeks. As their capsule separated from the service module prior to reentry, Disaster struck. An equalization valve jarred open, venting all cabin air into the vacuum of space. Because they were not wearing pressurized suits, the three men suffered fatal asphyxiation. Recovery forces opened the landed capsule to find those three men dead in their seats.
